records.source: רַנְּנ֣וּ צַ֭דִּיקִים בַּֽיהוָ֑ה לַ֝יְשָׁרִ֗ים נָאוָ֥ה תְהִלָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Shout for joy, righteous [ones], in YHWH; for the upright praise [is] fitting.
pieces: Sing for joy in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you righteous; praise suits those who are upright.

L.1: Shout for joy, righteous [ones], in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; for the upright praise [is] fitting.

R.1: People who do what is right, shout for joy because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! It is right for honest people to praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.reason: Psalm 33 is one of the few psalms in Psalms 1-41 with no title. Its first words take up the last line of Psalm 32 ("shout for joy ... righteous"), and it is a song of praise to the LORD as Creator and ruler of the nations.

decisions.choice: fitting: what is right and becoming
decisions.reason: Praise suits the upright (147:1): it is the natural response of those who are right with God.
Readable says whom the praise is for.

records.heading: Praise the Creator who rules the nations

records.source: הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה בְּכִנּ֑וֹר בְּנֵ֥בֶל עָ֝שׂ֗וֹר זַמְּרוּ־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Give thanks to YHWH with [the] lyre; with [the] harp of ten make music to him.
pieces: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the lyre; play music for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the ten-stringed harp.

L.2: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with [the] lyre; with [the] harp of ten [strings] make music to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.2: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with music on the lyre. Play songs for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on a harp with ten strings.

decisions.choice: lyre and harp: two stringed instruments
decisions.reason: The kinnor was a lyre, a light instrument held in the hands; the nevel was a larger stringed instrument. Both were played in worship (1 Chronicles 15:16; 2 Samuel 6:5).

decisions.choice: harp of ten: a ten-stringed harp
decisions.reason: The word "ten" stands beside "harp" and is taken as describing it (144:9); in 92:4 the two are named side by side.

records.source: שִֽׁירוּ־ל֭וֹשִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ הֵיטִ֥יבוּ נַ֝גֵּ֗ן בִּתְרוּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: Sing to him a new song; do well [at] playing with a shout of joy.
pieces: Sing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a new song; play your best, with shouts of joy.

L.3: Sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a new song; do well [at] playing with a shout of joy.

R.3: Sing a new song to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Play your instruments well, and shout with joy.

decisions.choice: a new song: fresh praise for what God has done
decisions.reason: A new song answers a new act of God (40:4; 96:1; 98:1; Isaiah 42:10).

decisions.choice: shout of joy: a loud ringing cry
decisions.reason: The word (teru'ah) is the shout or trumpet blast of a festival or a battle (Numbers 10:5; 2 Samuel 6:15).

records.source: כִּֽי־יָשָׁ֥ר דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה וְכָל־מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: For upright [is] the word of YHWH, and all his work [is] in faithfulness.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s word is right, and all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness.

L.4: For upright [is] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work [is done] in faithfulness.

R.4: Everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is right. You can count on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD: what he says and commands
decisions.reason: His word is both his promise and the command by which he made the world (verses 6 and 9).
The word ('emunah) means firmness, being dependable; all he does can be relied on.
Readable says what faithfulness means for people (m2).

records.source: אֹ֭הֵב צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט חֶ֥סֶד יְ֝הוָ֗ה מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: [He is] loving righteousness and justice; of the loyal love of YHWH the earth is full.
pieces: He loves what is right and just; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s loyal love fills the whole earth.

L.5: [He] loves righteousness and justice; of the loyal love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the earth is full.

R.5: He loves what is right and fair. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s faithful love is everywhere on earth.

decisions.choice: righteousness and justice: what is right and fair
decisions.reason: The pair (tsedaqah and mishpat) describes right order in the world, and is what kings were to uphold (Jeremiah 22:15; 2 Samuel 8:15).

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps its commitments
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that is faithful to a bond and goes beyond what is owed: the LORD's commitment to his people, shown in kindness and rescue (Exodus 34:6-7).
As in Psalms 1-12: "loyal love" keeps both the love and the faithfulness of the word; Readable says "faithful love".

decisions.choice: loving: the LORD is the one who loves
decisions.reason: The word is a participle with no subject; the LORD of verse 4 is meant, and his name follows in the next line.

records.source: בִּדְבַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה שָׁמַ֣יִם נַעֲשׂ֑וּ וּבְר֥וּחַ פִּ֝֗יו כָּל־צְבָאָֽם׃
records.gloss: By the word of YHWH [the] heavens were made, and by the breath of his mouth all their host.
pieces: The heavens were made at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s word, and the breath of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth made all their array of stars.

L.6: By the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [the] heavens were made, and by the breath of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth all their host.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke, and the sky was made. He breathed out a word, and all the stars came to be.

decisions.choice: By the word ... the heavens were made: Genesis 1
decisions.reason: God made the world by speaking: "And God said, Let there be ..." (Genesis 1:3, 6, 14). Genesis 2:1 also speaks of the heavens "and all their host".

decisions.choice: the breath of his mouth: his spoken word
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) means breath, wind or spirit. In parallel with "word" it is the breath that carries the word (Isaiah 11:4).
The host of heaven is its great company, usually the stars (Isaiah 40:26), sometimes the angels (1 Kings 22:19).

decisions.choice: array of stars (B); all the stars (R)
decisions.reason: "Host" now means someone who receives guests; Balanced and Readable say what is meant (m3).

records.source: כֹּנֵ֣ס כַּ֭נֵּד מֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם נֹתֵ֖ן בְּאֹצָר֣וֹת תְּהוֹמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Gathering like a heap the waters of the sea, putting in storehouses [the] deeps.
pieces: He heaps up the waters of the sea like a mound and keeps the ocean depths in storerooms.

L.7: [He] gathers as a heap the waters of the sea; [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] puts [the] deeps in storehouses.

R.7: He piles up the water of the sea like a heap. He keeps the deep oceans in storerooms.

decisions.choice: like a heap: the waters piled up
decisions.reason: With the vowels of the Hebrew text the word means a heap, as when the sea stood up at the Exodus (Exodus 15:8; Joshua 3:13). The ancient Greek translation read the same letters as "wineskin": God holds the sea as in a bottle. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: storehouses for the deeps: the waters under God's control
decisions.reason: The deep waters, which the ancient world feared as chaos, are kept in God's stores like grain or treasure (Job 38:22; Jeremiah 10:13).
The Hebrew uses participles with no subject ("gathering ..., putting ..."); Literal brackets the subject.

records.source: יִֽירְא֣וּ מֵ֭יְהוָה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ מִמֶּ֥נּוּ יָ֝ג֗וּרוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Let all the earth fear YHWH; of him let all [the] inhabitants of [the] world be in awe.
pieces: Let the whole earth fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; let everyone who lives in the world tremble with awe before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.8: Let all the earth fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe.

R.8: Everyone on earth should have deep respect for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. All the people in the world should honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with awe.

decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to take him seriously as God: reverence, awe and obedience (Proverbs 1:7). The parallel verb (gur) is to be in awe or to dread.

decisions.choice: all the earth: all its people
decisions.reason: "All the earth" means the people living on it, as the second line says.
Readable gives the sense of the fear meant here (m1).

records.source: כִּ֤י ה֣וּא אָמַ֣ר וַיֶּ֑הִי הֽוּא־צִ֝וָּ֗ה וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽד׃
records.gloss: For he spoke and it was; he commanded and it stood.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} only had to speak, and it was; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the command, and there it stood.

L.9: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke, and it came to be; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded, and it stood.

R.9: He spoke, and the world was there. He gave an order, and it stood in its place.

decisions.choice: he spoke and it was: Genesis 1
decisions.reason: As in verse 6: "God said ... and it was so" (Genesis 1:9, 11).
The Hebrew adds the pronoun twice for emphasis: it was he who spoke.
What he made stands in place and lasts, as his plans stand in verse 11.
Balanced brings out the ease and power of the word (m2).
Readable names what came to be, the world of verses 6-8.

records.source: יְֽהוָ֗ה הֵפִ֥יר עֲצַת־גּוֹיִ֑ם הֵ֝נִ֗יא מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת עַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: YHWH has broken [the] counsel of nations; he has frustrated [the] plans of peoples.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brings the schemes of nations to nothing; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blocks what the peoples plan.

L.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has broken the counsel of [the] nations; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has frustrated the plans of [the] peoples.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} stops the plans of the nations. He keeps peoples from doing what they plan.

decisions.choice: has broken, has frustrated: what the LORD does
decisions.reason: The past forms state what the LORD has done and always does; Balanced and Readable use the present.
The same two words return in verse 11 for the LORD's own purposes: theirs fail, his stand.

records.source: עֲצַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם תַּעֲמֹ֑ד מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת לִ֝בּ֗וֹ לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃
records.gloss: The counsel of YHWH forever stands, the plans of his heart to generation and generation.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s purpose stands firm forever, and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart lasts through every generation.

L.11: The counsel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stands forever, the plans of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart to generation and generation.

R.11: But what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} decides will last forever. His plans will go on for every generation.

decisions.choice: counsel, plans: set against those of verse 10
decisions.reason: The same words as in verse 10; the contrast is plain without a "but".

decisions.choice: to generation and generation: through all time
decisions.reason: The doubled word means one generation after another, without end.
Readable marks the contrast with verse 10 (m1).

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֣י הַ֭גּוֹי אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו הָעָ֓ם׀בָּחַ֖ר לְנַחֲלָ֣ה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is] the nation whose God [is] YHWH, the people he has chosen for an inheritance for himself.
pieces: How blessed is the nation that has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as its God, the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own possession!

L.12: How blessed [is] the nation whose God [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the people [whom] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen as an inheritance for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}!

R.12: Life is truly good for the nation that has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as its God. He chose that people to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} very own.

decisions.reason: As in 1:1.
An inheritance is property that belongs to a family for good. Israel is the LORD's own share (Deuteronomy 32:9; Exodus 19:5).
The people chosen by the LORD is Israel, set against the nations of verse 10.
"Inheritance" suggests receiving something after a death; Balanced and Readable say what is meant (m2).

records.source: מִ֭שָּׁמַיִם הִבִּ֣יט יְהוָ֑ה רָ֝אָ֗ה אֶֽת־כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: From [the] heavens YHWH looks; he sees all [the] children of humankind.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} looks out from heaven and sees every human being.

L.13: From [the] heavens {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looks; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees all the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} looks at the earth from heaven. He sees every person there.

decisions.reason: As in 11:4, the phrase (bene ha'adam) means human beings.
The LORD's throne is in heaven (11:4); from there he sees all that happens.

decisions.choice: children of humankind, with "sons of men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 11:4.

records.source: מִֽמְּכוֹן־שִׁבְתּ֥וֹ הִשְׁגִּ֑יחַ אֶ֖ל כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: From [the] place of his dwelling he gazes on all [the] inhabitants of the earth,
pieces: From the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye on everyone who lives on the earth,

L.14: From the place of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gazes on all the inhabitants of the earth,

R.14: From {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home in heaven, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} watches all the people who live on the earth.

decisions.choice: the place of his dwelling: his fixed abode
decisions.reason: The word (makon) is a firm, set place; the verb can mean to dwell or to sit enthroned (1 Kings 8:39).
A rare verb (shagach) for looking out intently (Song 2:9).
Readable names the place from verse 13.

records.source: הַיֹּצֵ֣ר יַ֣חַד לִבָּ֑ם הַ֝מֵּבִ֗ין אֶל־כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: the one forming together their heart, the one discerning to all their deeds.
pieces: the one who shaped every one of their hearts and who notices everything they do.

L.15: the one who forms their hearts all alike, who gives heed to all their deeds.

R.15: He made the hearts of all people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} understands everything they do.

decisions.choice: the one forming ... the one discerning: the LORD of verse 14
decisions.reason: The two participles describe the one who looks down in verses 13-14; the sentence runs on from verse 14.
The verb (yatsar) is used of a potter and of God forming the first human (Genesis 2:7). The one who made the heart knows it.
The word (yachad) means together or alike; he formed the hearts of all people.

records.source: אֵֽין־הַ֭מֶּלֶךְ נוֹשָׁ֣ע בְּרָב־חָ֑יִל גִּ֝בּ֗וֹר לֹֽא־יִנָּצֵ֥ל בְּרָב־כֹּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: There is not the king saved by greatness of an army; a warrior is not delivered by greatness of strength.
pieces: No king wins the day because his army is large; no warrior escapes because his strength is great.

L.16: The king is not saved by [the] greatness of an army; a warrior is not delivered by greatness of strength.

R.16: A king is not saved just because he has a big army. A strong soldier is not rescued just because he is strong.

decisions.reason: In battle, to be saved (yasha') is to come through and win. Victory belongs to the LORD (verse 17; 20:7-8).
The word (chayil) can mean strength, wealth or an army; with "king" it means his forces.

records.source: שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭סּוּס לִתְשׁוּעָ֑ה וּבְרֹ֥ב חֵ֝יל֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּֽט׃
records.gloss: A lie [is] the horse for victory, and by the greatness of its strength it does not rescue.
pieces: The horse is a deceptive hope for victory; with all its great strength it saves no one.

L.17: A lie [is] the horse for victory, and by the greatness of its strength it does not rescue.

R.17: Horses cannot win a battle for you. They may be strong, but they cannot save anyone.

decisions.choice: the horse: the power of war chariots and cavalry
decisions.reason: Horses meant military strength, which Israel's kings were warned not to trust (Deuteronomy 17:16; 20:8; Isaiah 31:1).

decisions.choice: a lie: a hope that lets you down
decisions.reason: The word (sheqer) means falsehood; to trust a horse for victory is to trust something that will fail.
The word (teshu'ah) is rescue or salvation; in a battle it is victory.

decisions.choice: cannot win a battle for you
alternatives: is a false hope for victory
decisions.reason: Readable states the point plainly (m2).

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה עֵ֣ין יְ֭הוָה אֶל־יְרֵאָ֑יו לַֽמְיַחֲלִ֥ים לְחַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Look, [the] eye of YHWH [is] to those fearing him, to those who wait for his loyal love,
pieces: Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keeps watch over those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who wait with hope for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love,

L.18: Look, the eye of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] on those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, on those who wait for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love,

R.18: Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} watches over people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They trust {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love.

decisions.choice: the eye of the LORD: his watchful care
decisions.reason: As in 32:8: his eye rests on them for good.
The verb (yachal) means to wait with expectation.

decisions.choice: Look: in contrast to the horse and the army
decisions.reason: The word (hinneh) points to the true source of rescue after verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps its commitments
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that is faithful to a bond and goes beyond what is owed: the LORD's commitment to his people, shown in kindness and rescue (Exodus 34:6-7).
As in Psalms 1-12: "loyal love" keeps both the love and the faithfulness of the word; Readable says "faithful love".
As in verse 8.

records.source: לְהַצִּ֣יל מִמָּ֣וֶת נַפְשָׁ֑ם וּ֝לְחַיּוֹתָ֗ם בָּרָעָֽב׃
records.gloss: to deliver from death their soul and to keep them alive in famine.
pieces: to save their lives from death and to keep them living through famine.

L.19: to deliver their soul from death and to keep them alive in famine.

R.19: He rescues them from death. When there is no food, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps them alive.

decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the living person, here their life itself.

decisions.choice: to deliver ... to keep alive: why the LORD watches
decisions.reason: The sentence from verse 18 goes on to say what his watchful eye is for.
Balanced and Readable say what nefesh means here (m1).

records.source: נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ חִכְּתָ֣ה לַֽיהוָ֑ה עֶזְרֵ֖נוּ וּמָגִנֵּ֣נוּ הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: Our soul waits for YHWH; our help and our shield [is] he.
pieces: With all our being we wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who helps us and shields us.

L.20: Our soul waits for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; our help and our shield [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}.

R.20: We are waiting for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to act. He helps us and protects us like a shield.

decisions.reason: "Our soul" (nefesh) is the whole self: we wait with our whole being.
As in 3:4; 18:3: God himself is the defense of his people.
Readable says what they wait for: the LORD's help.

records.source: כִּי־ב֭וֹ יִשְׂמַ֣ח לִבֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֤י בְשֵׁ֖ם קָדְשׁ֣וֹ בָטָֽחְנוּ׃
records.gloss: For in him our heart rejoices, for in [the] name of his holiness we have trusted.
pieces: Our hearts are glad in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because we have put our trust in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name.

L.21: For in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} our heart is glad, for in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name we have trusted.

R.21: We are happy because of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. We trust {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the holy God.

decisions.choice: his holy name: the LORD himself as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person; to trust in his name is to trust him (20:8).

decisions.choice: we have trusted: a settled trust
decisions.reason: The past form describes trust already placed and still held.
Readable says what the name stands for (m1).

records.source: יְהִֽי־חַסְדְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ כַּ֝אֲשֶׁ֗ר יִחַ֥לְנוּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Let your loyal love, YHWH, be on us, just as we have waited for you.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love be over us, in keeping with our hope in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.22: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be upon us, just as we have waited for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.22: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show us {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love, because we are waiting and hoping for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps its commitments
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that is faithful to a bond and goes beyond what is owed: the LORD's commitment to his people, shown in kindness and rescue (Exodus 34:6-7).
As in Psalms 1-12: "loyal love" keeps both the love and the faithfulness of the word; Readable says "faithful love".

decisions.choice: just as: in keeping with our hope
decisions.reason: The words (ka'asher) ask that God's love match the hope they have placed in him; they also give the reason for the request.

decisions.choice: we have waited: we have hoped
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 18: the psalm ends where those who wait for his love are watched over.
